summary: House Ways and Means Republicans advanced a bill directing the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission to restate its methodology for estimating Medicare Advantage overpayments in a way critics say would favor insurers over a stricter apples-to-apples comparison with traditional Medicare.

headline: White House orders $500 refunds to ACA exchange enrollees over fee overcharges
summary: The administration announced roughly $500 rebates to nearly a million people enrolled in federal ACA exchanges, tied to user fees collected to fund exchange operations that regulators determined had overcharged enrollees.

headline: Beijing extends first-ever recapitalization to state insurers
summary: China's government included state-owned insurers for the first time in a roughly $53.6 billion capital injection program alongside state banks, though analysts noted the relatively modest insurer allocation reflects already-healthy capital positions.

headline: China proposes fivefold hike in minimum insurer capital requirements
summary: China's National Financial Regulatory Administration released a draft revision to the Insurance Law that would raise insurers' minimum registered capital roughly fivefold, from CNY200 million to CNY1 billion (about $149 million).

headline: AI medical-liability insurtech Indigo raises $50 million Series B
summary: Indigo, an AI-driven platform underwriting medical professional liability coverage, closed a $50 million Series B round to expand its data-driven risk assessment tools for healthcare providers.

headline: Embedded-finance player Parafin extends reach into auto dealer software
summary: Parafin partnered with dealer-technology provider Tekion to embed its Pay Over Time financing product into Tekion Pay, letting auto dealerships split business invoices into biweekly installments instead of paying upfront.

headline: Health systems keep cutting jobs as Medicaid reimbursement pressure bites
summary: UMass Memorial Health's Community Healthlink division moved to lay off 231 positions and close programs effective September 16, part of a wider 2026 wave of health-system job cuts driven by reduced Medicaid reimbursement and rising uncompensated care costs.

headline: 401(k) balances hit record highs as long-tenured savers cross $270,000
summary: An analysis of more than 55 million retirement accounts found women continuously enrolled in a 401(k) for at least five years reached an average balance of $273,400 in Q2 2026, while millennial balances climbed 14.2% year-over-year to $94,300.

headline: EU regulators press for AI-risk oversight as EIOPA chief's term is extended
summary: The EU's three financial supervisory authorities called on banks, insurers and investment firms to recalibrate ICT risk controls for frontier AI models, while the Council of the EU separately extended EIOPA chair Petra Hielkema's mandate for a second five-year term starting September 1.

headline: US retirement assets climb to $51.2 trillion as markets rally in Q2 2026
summary: The Investment Company Institute's latest quarterly data shows total US retirement assets rose 7.9% from March to reach $51.2 trillion by June 30, 2026, with $10.8 trillion held specifically in 401(k) plans.

headline: Most 401(k) recordkeepers still lack broad student loan repayment integration, survey finds
summary: PLANSPONSOR's 2026 Recordkeeping Survey found only one-fifth of responding recordkeepers let plan sponsors choose among multiple integrated student loan repayment programs, while nearly a third offer none at all.

headline: Rick Case Enterprises settles 401(k) class action over recordkeeper transition losses
summary: Rick Case Enterprises has agreed to settle a proposed class action brought by 401(k) participants who alleged they lost significant retirement savings when the company changed recordkeepers.

headline: AIG plans to lean further into private assets as investment income growth slows
summary: AIG is increasing its allocation to private assets to help offset softer net investment income, with the insurer not expecting income growth to reaccelerate until 2027.

headline: RIA M&A activity tops $100 billion in assets already this year
summary: Markets Group reports that registered investment adviser M&A has already moved more than $100 billion in assets in 2026, underscoring the record pace of consolidation across the wealth management industry.

headline: Hightower, Carson Group and AlphaCore extend record-setting RIA dealmaking spree
summary: Hightower's Signature Wealth unit added a $1.6 billion Boston-area firm, Carson Group closed a 50-office deal with Elios Financial Group, and AlphaCore launched a family-office unit via a $5 billion acquisition, part of what is shaping up to be a record year for RIA M&A.

headline: AI wealth-transfer platform Luminary raises $22 million Series A
summary: Luminary, which turns static estate-planning documents into structured data for advisors and trust companies, raised a $22 million Series A led by Ten Coves Capital, bringing total funding to nearly $32 million and supporting more than $500 billion in client assets.

headline: US P&C insurers post $31.7 billion underwriting gain in first half of 2026
summary: Insurance Journal reports the US property/casualty industry's net underwriting gain jumped to $31.7 billion in H1 2026 from $11.6 billion a year earlier, even as premium growth slowed to 2.1% amid a widening split between property and casualty-line performance.

headline: Charles Taylor acquires Ohio-based third-party administrator Matrix Companies
summary: Global claims and TPA services provider Charles Taylor has acquired the Matrix Companies, an Ohio-based third-party administrator, expanding its US claims-handling footprint.

headline: TRISTAR expands with acquisition of New Jersey third-party administrator
summary: Claims and risk-management firm TRISTAR is acquiring a New Jersey-based third-party administrator, continuing the wave of consolidation among regional TPA and claims-services firms.

headline: Davies strikes strategic claims partnership with Brown & Brown in North America
summary: Claims and services group Davies has signed a deal with Brown & Brown adding new claims and services capabilities to its North America business, establishing a long-term strategic partnership between the two firms.

headline: Fintech dealmaking stays hot with $850 million raised in a single week
summary: A separate FinTech Global roundup tallied more than $850 million raised across fintech financings in the week of September 18, 2026, reflecting continued investor appetite for the sector.

headline: White House to issue $500 ACA marketplace refunds to nearly a million enrollees
summary: The administration announced $500 refunds for close to a million people enrolled in the federal ACA exchanges, tied to what it called overcharges collected through user fees under the prior administration.

headline: Sanford Health and North Memorial Health complete merger, pledge $600 million Minnesota investment
summary: The two nonprofit systems finalized their combination on September 1, 2026, with Sanford Health committing more than $600 million to expand Maple Grove Hospital and modernize Robbinsdale Hospital, whose Level I trauma center status is guaranteed for at least a decade.

headline: Indian Bank eyes insurance and mutual fund partnerships, plans wealth management launch
summary: Indian Bank is exploring partnerships to enter the insurance and mutual fund businesses within 1.5 to 2 years and plans to launch wealth management services in the second half of FY27.

headline: FinTech Innovation Lab Asia-Pacific names 2026 cohort of eight startups
summary: The 13th edition of the FinTech Innovation Lab Asia-Pacific selected eight technology companies, including climate-underwriting startup WeavAir, to work directly with major banks and insurers across the region.

headline: Identity verification firm Jumio expands reusable digital ID into Asia-Pacific
summary: Jumio extended its reusable identity solution, selfie.DONE, into the Asia-Pacific region on September 15, 2026, as regional financial institutions push to streamline onboarding and compliance.

headline: Allianz Trade names new China CEO as Asia-Pacific leadership shuffles continue
summary: Allianz Trade appointed Scott Munafo as its China CEO effective September 1, 2026, part of a string of senior Asia-Pacific leadership moves across the region's insurers this month, including a new chief underwriting officer at MSIG Hong Kong.

headline: NAIC working group begins overhaul of market conduct regulation
summary: State insurance regulators' new Market Conduct Regulation Modernization Working Group is collecting broad industry input through 2026, aiming to deliver actionable recommendations on modernizing market-conduct oversight by year-end.

headline: US cyber insurance pricing stays soft even as third-party claims climb
summary: US cyber insurance premiums were roughly flat through the first part of 2026 after a long run of rate cuts, but a roughly 30% rise in third-party claims is pressuring loss ratios and clouding the outlook for insurers.

headline: Zurich returns to the catastrophe bond market with a new closed deal
summary: Zurich successfully closed a new catastrophe bond, marking its return to the cat bond market as insurers continue tapping capital markets for property catastrophe protection amid ample investor appetite.

headline: Consumers face another sharp jump in health insurance costs heading into 2027
summary: Analysts warn that health insurance costs are set to rise steeply again in 2027 as insurers pass through higher medical trend and the fading of enhanced ACA subsidies, prompting fresh guidance on how households can manage premiums.

headline: Major health insurers post strong second-quarter 2026 results as cost trend eases
summary: UnitedHealthcare, Elevance Health and peers reported improving medical cost ratios in Q2 2026, with UnitedHealthcare's medical cost ratio falling from 89.4% to 86.7% and Elevance posting roughly $1.5 billion in quarterly profit, prompting raised full-year guidance.

headline: AIG's general insurance CEO Lou Hancock to retire at year-end
summary: AIG confirmed that Lou Hancock will step down as chief executive of its general insurance business at the end of 2026, part of a broader wave of senior leadership transition at the carrier this year.

headline: Newly licensed Indian insurer Protec taps insureMO to build an AI-native core system
summary: Protec General Insurance, a newly licensed Indian carrier, selected middle-office platform insureMO to build an API-driven, AI-native insurance core as it prepares to scale retail and commercial lines across India.

headline: Apollo launches a private-credit fund aimed at UK defined contribution pension savers
summary: Apollo introduced a long-term asset fund giving UK defined contribution pension schemes semi-liquid access to a private credit portfolio spanning investment-grade, large-cap corporate lending and asset-backed finance.

headline: APAC insurers accelerate technology bets heading into 2026
summary: A regional roundup highlights how APAC insurers are leaning further into digital distribution, automation and AI tooling as they compete for growth in under-penetrated markets across the region.

headline: US insurers brace for major ISO general liability form changes
summary: Insurers are preparing operational and pricing adjustments ahead of significant 2026 revisions to ISO's general liability forms, which are expected to reshape coverage language and underwriting workflows industry-wide.

headline: Greenfield Asian hospitals build AI-native records systems from the ground up
summary: Singapore's Woodlands Hospital and Taiwan's Taipei Veterans General Hospital are each using unified electronic medical record and interoperability architectures, unencumbered by legacy systems, to push AI use beyond clinical documentation.

headline: Sun Life and Wilton Re strike life and annuity reinsurance partnership
summary: The two insurers announced a strategic tie-up combining Wilton Re's liability management expertise with Sun Life's insurance and asset management capabilities across life and annuity reinsurance.

headline: WealthAi rolls out AI operating system for independent financial advisers
summary: The new WealthAi for Advisors product bundles meeting notes, client management, document generation and compliance into one AI-driven platform, with beta testers reporting roughly a 60% cut in time spent on routine client administration.

headline: AI-focused insurtechs dominate funding as early-stage deals cool
summary: AI-centered insurtechs pulled in the bulk of Q2 2026 venture funding, with earth-imagery startup ICEYE alone raising a roughly $520 million Series F, even as the number of early-stage deals slowed sharply.

headline: UCare moves to exit the Medicare Advantage market for 2026
summary: Minnesota nonprofit insurer UCare asked CMS to mutually terminate its Medicare Advantage plans, citing rising medical costs and broader strain within the MA market, and is laying off employees as a result.

headline: US annuity sales notch another record first half, RILA leads growth
summary: Finalized LIMRA data show second-quarter 2026 US annuity sales around $121 billion (revised down slightly from an initial $123.9B estimate), extending an 11-quarter streak above $100 billion and pushing first-half 2026 sales to a record $231.3 billion, with registered index-linked annuities (RILAs) growing fastest.

headline: Legacy Marketing and Malibu Life USA team up on new indexed annuity line
summary: Legacy Marketing Group struck a distribution partnership with Malibu Life USA to bring two new fixed indexed annuity products, PillarMark and SpireMark, to market through independent agents starting this month, issued by Malibu's Texas-domiciled carrier TruSpire.

headline: State AI-governance rules for insurers reach a tipping point in 2026
summary: Adoption of the NAIC's AI Model Bulletin has spread to roughly 25 US states as of mid-2026, with several more in progress, pushing carriers to build documented AI governance, testing and monitoring programs for underwriting and claims models as a new multistate examiner tool pilots across a dozen states.

headline: Luxembourg insurer OneLife completes CEO handover
summary: Cross-border life insurer OneLife confirmed Cédric Lootvoet as its new Chief Executive Officer effective September 1, 2026, succeeding Bruno Valersteinas after Lootvoet had spent roughly nine months as Deputy CEO preparing for the transition.

headline: Full plan terminations now drive most pension risk transfer deals
summary: October Three's 2026 PRT Trends survey found plan terminations accounted for two-thirds of pension risk transfer transactions in the first half of 2026, with buy-in premiums up sharply even as total buyout dollar volume cooled from a strong 2025 finish, and carriers reporting less worry about PRT litigation than a year ago.

headline: DOL floats safe harbor for putting alternative assets into 401(k) menus
summary: The Department of Labor's proposed rule, issued March 31, 2026 under a 2025 White House executive order, would give plan fiduciaries a six-factor "prudent process" safe harbor for adding private equity, real estate and other alternative investments as 401(k) and 403(b) designated investment options.

headline: Aging Asia-Pacific populations push pension providers toward income-focused products
summary: Amundi's research team flagged that rapidly aging populations in Japan, China, Australia and South Korea are shifting demand from pure accumulation toward decumulation and retirement-income products, as state and workplace pension systems in the region struggle to keep pace.

headline: Grayscale pushes crypto further into mainstream advisor portfolios
summary: Grayscale rolled out digital-asset model portfolios for financial advisors in mid-September 2026, giving wealth managers a packaged way to add crypto exposure to client accounts as digital assets keep edging into traditional asset-management platforms.

headline: BNP Paribas Asset Management installs four new co-CIOs
summary: BNP Paribas Asset Management named four new Chief Investment Officers, including Guy Davies as Deputy Global Head of Investments and CIO for fundamental active equity and Robinson Rouchié as CIO for systematic and quantitative investments, effective September 1, 2026, reporting to global investments head Rob Gambi as part of the firm's "AMplify 2030" plan.

headline: AGF's August AUM snapshot shows steady asset growth
summary: Canadian asset manager AGF reported total assets under management and fee-earning assets of roughly $74.2 billion as of August 31, 2026, offering an early read on how markets and flows treated mid-tier managers heading into the fall.

headline: India's wealth management market on track to more than double by the mid-2030s
summary: India's wealth-management industry is projected to roughly 2.5x to about $436 billion by 2034, fueled by a 90% four-year jump in dollar-millionaire households and mutual fund AUM approaching Rs 78 lakh crore, according to industry estimates cited in early September coverage.

headline: SEC pushes forward on adviser recordkeeping and fiduciary-conduct rulemaking
summary: The SEC published a proposed rule amendment in the Federal Register on September 10 updating books-and-records requirements for investment advisers, part of a broader FY2026 exam agenda emphasizing fiduciary standards, conflict-of-interest disclosure and Regulation S-P cybersecurity compliance.

headline: Chicago RIA Choreo taps another Edelman veteran for newly created executive post
summary: Choreo named Kelly O'Donnell as its first chief people and transformation officer, marking the fourth Edelman Financial Engines alum hired into a C-suite role at the RIA in about a year; she will oversee HR, brand and the integration of acquired firms.

headline: Mapfre's buyout of Safety Insurance clears key antitrust hurdle
summary: The regulatory waiting period on Mapfre's acquisition of Safety Insurance Group expired on September 14, clearing the way for Safety to become a wholly owned Mapfre subsidiary after shareholder materials were mailed the same week.

headline: US P&C insurers post stronger profits even as premium growth cools sharply
summary: Industry-wide net underwriting gains more than doubled to $31.7 billion in the first half of 2026, even as net written premium growth slowed to about 2.1% from 5.2% a year earlier, with personal auto and commercial property rates softening while liability and casualty losses kept worsening.

headline: UK consolidator Clear Group buys specialist Lloyd's wholesale broker
summary: Clear Group acquired Newman Pearce & Partners, a 24-person Lloyd's wholesale broker whose revenue grew from about £5m to £7m in the past year, as part of Clear's push to deepen its London market wholesale broking presence.

headline: Specialty insurer Mosaic rolls out AI-driven underwriting platform for SMEs
summary: Mosaic Insurance launched a digital underwriting system called HALO that combines broker trading activity, underwriting decisions and portfolio outcomes in one environment, aimed at speeding up delivery of complex specialty products to small and midsize business customers.

headline: Asia-Pacific insurance dealmaking cools even as India and Malaysia buck the trend
summary: Broader M&A activity across Asia-Pacific's insurance and broking sector slowed in the second quarter of 2026, even as India and Malaysia each recorded major multi-million-dollar transactions, underscoring uneven momentum across the region's markets.

headline: Marsh names new global chief claims officer as it reshuffles claims leadership
summary: Marsh Risk appointed Chetna Gulati-Kapoor, a 20-year claims veteran who trained as a solicitor in India and the UK, as global chief claims officer effective September 1, succeeding Rob Powell, who moves up to chairman of global claims.

headline: AI-native claims TPA Elysian bolsters leadership with new claims strategy chief
summary: Elysian, a startup positioning itself as an AI-native third-party administrator for complex commercial claims, named industry veteran Armando Andrade as its Head of Claims Strategy, bringing over two decades of TPA and claims-operations experience from TheBest Claims Solutions.

headline: Zinnia adds whole-life product engine to its Zahara administration platform
summary: Life and annuity technology vendor Zinnia expanded its Zahara policy administration system with a new configurable whole-life chassis aimed at the final-expense market, letting carriers launch products in roughly three months as API-based, cloud-native administration continues replacing legacy batch systems.

headline: Wealthtech giant FNZ secures $450m top-up from existing backers
summary: Global wealth-management technology platform FNZ raised $450 million in new equity from long-standing institutional investors including CPP Investments and La Caisse, earmarking the funds for continued platform modernization, hiring and product expansion.

headline: UK broker JMG Group names Andrew Cunis to lead South and private-client business
summary: UK insurance broker consolidator JMG Group appointed industry veteran Andrew Cunis, who brings more than 22 years of experience, as chief executive of its South of England and private-client operations as the group continues regional expansion.

headline: AIG's top P&C executive Jon Hancock to step down at year-end
summary: AIG disclosed that General Insurance CEO Jon Hancock will retire December 31, 2026 and move into a senior advisory role reporting to CEO Eric Andersen, the latest in a string of leadership changes atop the carrier this year.

headline: Florida clears HCSC's absorption of Cigna's local Medicare business
summary: Florida's insurance commissioner signed off on Health Care Service Corp's acquisition of Cigna's HealthSpring Medicare Advantage operations in the state, one of the remaining state-level approvals needed to fully fold Cigna's Medicare book into HCSC.

headline: ACA enrollees hit with the subsidy cliff again as enhanced credits lapse
summary: With the pandemic-era enhanced premium tax credits gone as of January 1, 2026, the ACA's hard income cutoff for subsidy eligibility has returned, and marketplace insurers' median proposed rate increase for 2026 sits around 18-20%, pushing many middle-income households toward much higher net premiums.

headline: Big payers say AI-driven prior-auth cleanup is cutting transaction volume
summary: The six largest publicly traded insurers report they've standardized documentation for more than half their prior-authorization requests under an industry pledge, and sector-wide prior-auth volume has fallen about 11% over a 10-month stretch as automated, standardized workflows take hold.

headline: Employer medical plan cost inflation eases slightly across Asia-Pacific
summary: Brokers report that year-over-year medical trend increases for corporate health plans across Asia-Pacific markets are moderating somewhat in 2026 compared with recent years, though costs remain elevated as insurers cite an aging population and rising private-care demand.

headline: Hospital margins keep sliding as expenses outrun reimbursement
summary: System-wide operating margins fell roughly 5% nationally in early 2026 versus a year earlier, with rising bad debt and uncompensated care, soft government reimbursement and Medicare Advantage payment friction squeezing smaller hospitals hardest while the largest nonprofit systems hold up better.

headline: Taiwan's hospitals roll out agentic AI at scale with NVIDIA and Foxconn
summary: Under a $1.5B 'Healthy Taiwan' push, Foxconn and the island's leading medical centers are deploying NVIDIA-powered clinical agents for tasks like ECG screening, cancer subtyping and real-time procedural support, covering over 14 million patient encounters a year.

headline: Ambient-AI vendor Suki pushes past documentation into standalone dictation tools
summary: Clinical scribe company Suki is broadening its ambient AI suite with a modular, standalone dictation product for EHRs, part of a wider push by ambient-documentation vendors to extend beyond note-taking into fuller clinical workflow support.

headline: CMS locks in more than 5,500 specialists for its mandatory 2027 payment model
summary: CMS released the final participant roster for its new Ambulatory Specialty Model, compelling 5,556 specialists treating heart failure and low back pain in selected regions into value-based payment starting January 1, 2027, with the program running five performance years.

headline: ChristianaCare taps Jenn Schwartz as next CEO
summary: Delaware-based ChristianaCare named Jenn Schwartz as its incoming chief executive, succeeding longtime CEO Janice Nevin, who retired September 1, 2026, as part of a broader wave of health-system leadership turnover this year.

headline: Indian insurer stocks jump on expected crackdown on distributor commissions
summary: Shares of HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life, SBI Life and Max Financial rallied as much as 5% after reports that India's insurance regulator IRDAI is preparing a consultation paper to cap or reduce commissions paid to banks and other distributors, a move investors expect to lower acquisition costs and lift margins.

headline: India's pension regulator overhauls NPS fees and lets banks sponsor pension funds
summary: PFRDA cleared scheduled banks to sponsor and run National Pension System pension funds under a new slab-based investment-management fee structure from April 2026, and separately clarified a revised CRA charge structure for NPS accounts taking effect July 1, 2026.

headline: CVC finishes rollup of credit manager Marathon into new CVC-Marathon platform
summary: CVC Capital Partners completed its roughly $1.6 billion acquisition of Marathon Asset Management, rebranding the combined credit business as CVC-Marathon and pushing CVC Credit's fee-paying AUM to around €61 billion.

headline: Wealth-manager tie-ups keep asset and wealth management dealmaking hot
summary: PwC's mid-2026 US deals outlook found asset and wealth management M&A holding up despite macro uncertainty, with first-quarter 2026 deal volume hitting 109 transactions - the highest quarterly total in two years - and wealth-management consolidation driving roughly three-quarters of that activity.

headline: RIA consolidation wave keeps building as serial acquirers hit new AUM milestones
summary: Nationwide RIA deal volume has climbed roughly 40% year-over-year through mid-2026, with active platform buyers like Beacon Pointe, Savant and Mercer Advisors racking up multiple tuck-in acquisitions this year while a smaller number of platform-scale deals account for an outsized share of assets changing hands.

headline: Fintech investors keep favoring wealthtech in a blockbuster funding week
summary: More than $1.3 billion was raised across a dozen fintech deals in a single week in early September, extending a 2026 pattern where investors are writing fewer but much larger checks into wealth management, financial infrastructure and enterprise automation startups.

headline: India overhauls insurer capital and ownership rules under new reform package
summary: IRDAI approved amended regulations covering insurer registration, capital structure and amalgamation, part of a broader 2026 reform push under the new insurance-law amendment act that also enabled two insurers to raise foreign ownership above the old 74% cap following the move to permit 100% FDI.

headline: Aon strikes $17 billion deal for rival broker USI to bulk up in the middle market
summary: Aon agreed to buy USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17 billion in cash, following its earlier NFP purchase, aiming to build a leading middle-market platform and expand access to the excess-and-surplus lines market; USI's CEO will become Aon's global middle-market chief once the deal closes in Q4 2026.

headline: Cyber-focused MGA Trivora lands growth capital from private equity backer
summary: Trivora Insurance, a specialty cyber MGA for small and mid-sized businesses, secured a growth investment led by Carroll Street Capital, which also gets a board seat and a right of first refusal on future acquisition financing as Trivora expands into new specialty lines.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group buys Vermont retirement-plan TPA Future Planning Associates
summary: Retirement-plan administration consolidator Fiduciary Services Group acquired Future Planning Associates, a Vermont-based third-party administrator and recordkeeping firm, marking FSG's third TPA acquisition in about 14 months as consolidation continues in benefits administration.

headline: IRDAI finalizes feedback on proposed overhaul of TPA health-services rules
summary: India's insurance regulator IRDAI published its formal response to stakeholder comments on draft amendments to the Third Party Administrators (Health Services) Regulations, agreeing to clarify certificate-renewal requirements and cancellation procedures for TPAs after a public consultation that closed in mid-2026.

headline: Insurance software vendor Insurity elevates Jatin Atre to chief executive
summary: Insurance technology provider Insurity promoted Jatin Atre, who had served as president since January 2026, to chief executive officer, succeeding Jeff Clarke, as the company pushes to accelerate AI-powered products for brokers and carriers.

headline: State regulators wrap pilot of new AI governance exam tool for insurers
summary: NAIC's multistate pilot of its AI Systems Evaluation Tool, which gives market-conduct examiners a standardized way to probe insurers' algorithmic governance, has been running since January and concludes this month, reinforcing that existing insurance law applies however underwriting or claims decisions are automated.

headline: French digital health insurer Alan raises €480M to push into Canada
summary: Alan closed a Prosus-led Series G of roughly $550M at a €5.5B valuation, with Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan returning for a third round; the Paris-based carrier says it topped €800M in annualized revenue in Q1 2026 and is using the capital to scale its newly licensed Canadian health plan business.

headline: Cigna hands the CEO job to Brian Evanko as Cordani steps back
summary: The Cigna Group announced that President and COO Brian Evanko will succeed David Cordani as chief executive effective July 1, 2026, with Cordani shifting to executive chair — one of several long-tenured payer CEOs to exit this year.

headline: Clinical AI keeps pulling outsized venture dollars in digital health's rebound
summary: US digital health startups raised $7.4B in the first half of 2026, up from $6.4B a year earlier, with clinical-workflow AI a standout category; radiology-AI platform Aidoc alone landed its second $150M check in under a year.

headline: 401(k) and 403(b) balances hit record highs as savers stay the course
summary: Fidelity's Q2 2026 retirement analysis found average 401(k) balances grew roughly 10.5% quarter-over-quarter, pushing 401(k), 403(b) and IRA balances to new highs as participants maintained contribution rates despite market swings.

headline: Sequoia Financial Group buys $2.3 billion Colorado RIA BSW Wealth Partners
summary: Sequoia Financial Group announced the acquisition of BSW Wealth Partners, a roughly $2.3 billion AUM registered investment advisor, expanding Sequoia's footprint in Colorado as RIA roll-up activity continues at a rapid pace in 2026.

headline: Aon to acquire USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17 billion
summary: Aon confirmed a definitive agreement to acquire USI Insurance Services from private equity owner KKR for $17 billion, extending Aon's push into the US middle market following its 2024 purchase of NFP and adding USI's wholesale MGA/MGU capabilities.

headline: AI-native small-business health benefits brokerage Corridor launches with $25 million seed round
summary: Corridor, an AI-native benefits brokerage aimed at closing the gap between the health coverage options available to large employers versus small businesses, launched with a $25 million seed round led by Bain Capital Ventures with participation from BoxGroup and Definition Capital.

headline: WTW warns UK employer health insurance costs set to jump more than 10% in 2026
summary: A WTW analysis projects UK private medical insurance costs for employers will rise over 10% in 2026, as elevated medical inflation driven by expensive oncology treatments and a surge in mental health claims continues to squeeze corporate health benefit budgets.

headline: FTC finds PBM specialty-drug markups generated $7.3 billion in excess revenue
summary: A Federal Trade Commission report found the largest pharmacy benefit managers marked up specialty generic drugs enough to generate more than $7.3 billion in excess revenue between 2017 and 2022, with PBM-affiliated pharmacies charging especially steep markups on cancer and HIV medications.

headline: Guthrie Clinic and UF Health deploy R1's AI-native utilization and revenue-cycle platform
summary: Guthrie Clinic and UF Health became early adopters of R1's Phare platform, an AI-powered tool that shifts utilization management from retrospective chart review to real-time clinical and financial decisioning as health systems scale enterprise AI beyond pilots.

headline: US P&C insurers post $31.7 billion underwriting gain in first half of 2026
summary: The US property/casualty industry's net underwriting gain nearly tripled to $31.7 billion in H1 2026 versus $11.6 billion a year earlier, while net written premium growth slowed to 2.1% as the market continues to soften and competition intensifies.

headline: Sapiens expands executive bench with new Chief Autonomous Enterprise Officer and CMO
summary: Core insurance software provider Sapiens International named Nazir Esmail as Chief Autonomous Enterprise Officer and Maggie Fox as Chief Marketing Officer, broadening its leadership team as it pushes further into AI-driven, autonomous insurance operations.

headline: AIG names Sierra Signorelli CEO of Americas and Global Personal Insurance as Zaffino steps back
summary: AIG appointed Sierra Signorelli, rejoining from Zurich, as Chief Executive Officer of Americas and Global Personal Insurance effective January 2027, while Peter Zaffino stepped down as Executive Chair and board member effective September 15, 2026.

headline: Fed's September rate hike gives fixed and indexed annuity crediting rates a lift
summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16 in a unanimous vote, and higher long-term yields are letting insurers offer more attractive crediting rates on fixed and fixed-indexed annuities while easing some reserve pressure.

headline: Prudential Singapore widens tied-agent advisory lineup to include wealth products
summary: Prudential Singapore said its roughly 5,400 tied-agency financial representatives will be able to offer unit trusts and other wealth-accumulation products starting in 2027, part of a push toward more holistic retirement and wealth advice.

headline: Insurers favor steady portfolio tilts over big shifts in Invesco's mid-2026 outlook
summary: Invesco's mid-year 2026 investment outlook for insurers argues for incremental portfolio evolution rather than wholesale shifts, with insurers keeping high-quality public credit as a core holding while selectively adding floating-rate and senior secured private assets.

headline: Stansberry Asset Management rebrands as Meristead Wealth, managing $1.4 billion
summary: Stansberry Asset Management officially relaunched as Meristead Wealth, a national RIA managing close to $1.4 billion in assets, reflecting a decade of growth since its 2016 founding and an expanded role helping clients manage and preserve wealth.

headline: Creative Planning to acquire $4.3 trillion institutional consultant RVK
summary: Creative Planning agreed to acquire Portland-based institutional investment consultant RVK, which advises roughly 200 clients including pension plans, endowments and insurers on $4.3 trillion in assets; the deal is expected to close in January 2027 with terms undisclosed.

headline: AI-led wealth platform Quartz raises £2.75 million pre-seed round
summary: UK wealthtech startup Quartz raised a £2.75 million pre-seed round to build an AI-led wealth management platform, joining a wave of early-stage funding for AI-native advisory tools.

headline: California adopts 6.6% workers' comp rate increase, below industry's ask
summary: California's insurance commissioner set a new advisory pure premium rate of $1.65 per $100 of payroll, a 6.6% increase effective September 1, 2026, well below the 10.4% increase the state's rating bureau had requested, citing rising medical costs and cumulative trauma claims.

headline: EU unveils Climate Insurance Alliance to close catastrophe protection gap
summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a new Climate Insurance Alliance bringing together insurers, investors, regulators and risk modelers to expand catastrophe coverage, after a summer of drought, wildfires and heatwaves left only about a quarter of losses privately insured.

headline: Cyber insurance rates fall for a fourth straight year as AI reshapes risk
summary: Swiss Re reported global cyber insurance rates fell about 5% in 2026, the fourth consecutive year of declines, as abundant capacity created a buyer's market even as AI amplifies ransomware and phishing risks; Swiss Re projects global cyber premiums reaching $16.4 billion this year.

headline: MGA deal activity accelerates as scale and specialization drive valuations
summary: Managing general agent M&A continues to surge as buyers pay up for scale and underwriting specialization, with specialty P&C carriers, MGAs and E&S businesses driving a growing share of overall insurance deal flow.

headline: Hong Kong's new insurance push puts fresh opportunities on brokers' radar
summary: A newly outlined Hong Kong insurance market plan is drawing broker attention to new lines and distribution opportunities as the territory looks to expand its position as a regional insurance hub.

headline: Circuit split emerges over ERISA preemption for TPA negligence claims
summary: A September fiduciary compliance update flagged a new circuit split after the Ninth Circuit allowed a healthcare provider's negligent-misrepresentation claim against a plan administrator to proceed past ERISA preemption in August, while the Sixth Circuit reached the opposite conclusion on similar facts days later.

headline: Insurers told faster AI adoption needs stronger governance, not less
summary: Industry commentary warns that as insurers speed up AI deployment in underwriting and claims, weak data governance is becoming the bigger risk, with surveys showing many commercial insurers still don't fully trust the data feeding their models.

headline: Better underwriting data seen as key lever against insurance fraud
summary: Commentary from FinTech Global argues that stronger underwriting data quality, rather than fraud detection tools alone, is the most effective way for insurers to catch fraudulent claims and applications before they are written.

headline: Insurers weigh whether AI can help close the climate protection gap
summary: A FinTech Global analysis examines whether AI-driven risk modeling and pricing tools can help insurers profitably extend coverage into regions facing rising climate-driven losses, rather than simply retreating from them.

headline: ISG research for mea Platform finds insurers ready to hand off repeatable work to AI
summary: Research commissioned by UK insurtech mea Platform from ISG found 83% of the global insurance market would support AI executing repeatable operational work, though 75% said they would only trust it within an insurance-specific or governed model.

headline: ACA insurers propose median 15% premium hike for 2027 in early filings
summary: Preliminary 2027 rate filings show ACA marketplace insurers proposing a median 15% premium increase, the second straight year of double-digit hikes, as insurers adjust to the expiration of enhanced federal subsidies and rising underlying medical costs.

headline: India weighs standardized treatment rates to rein in health insurance costs
summary: Indian policymakers are considering a broad health insurance overhaul, including standardized hospital treatment rates, uniform coverage rules and a wider nationwide claims platform, as medical inflation running at 12-14% a year strains affordability; a joint panel of regulators, insurers and hospitals is due to report by year-end.

headline: Hospital M&A rebounds sharply with 40 deals announced in first half of 2026
summary: Hospital mergers and acquisitions rebounded in the first half of 2026 with 40 deals announced, according to Kaufman Hall, a sharp pickup after 2025 saw only 46 deals all year, the smallest annual total in 15 years.

headline: Taipei Veterans General Hospital moves AI insights directly into clinical workflows
summary: The 3,000-bed Taipei Veterans General Hospital, newly validated at Stage 7 of the HIMSS EMR Adoption Model, is integrating AI-generated insights directly into clinician workflows using HL7 FHIR standards rather than treating AI as a bolt-on tool.

headline: Fed's September rate hike lifts annuity crediting rates as bond yields hit 19-year high
summary: The Fed raised the federal funds rate a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16, its first hike since 2023. Fixed annuity rates track long-term bond yields more than the Fed funds rate, and with the 10-year Treasury near 5%, a 19-year high, insurers have room to price more attractive crediting rates this week.

headline: FCA finds UK protection market delivers good outcomes but 58% of consumers still lack cover
summary: The FCA's final Pure Protection Market Study found the market largely works well for buyers, with high claims acceptance and low complaints, but flagged that 58% of consumers don't hold a pure protection policy. The regulator will pursue non-binding action on consumer awareness, the sales journey and innovation rather than new rules.

headline: Vanguard agrees to acquire RIA custodian Altruist
summary: Vanguard has agreed to acquire Altruist, one of the fastest-growing custodians serving registered investment advisers, in what Kitces' AdvisorTech roundup calls one of the most significant consolidation moves yet in the RIA custody and technology market.

headline: Five major RIA aggregator platforms reportedly weighing a sale
summary: Dakota reports that at least five of the largest RIA roll-up platforms are exploring potential sale processes, as private equity appetite for wealth-management consolidation continues to run hot heading into year-end.

headline: Edelman Financial Engines names Tina Wilson chief retirement officer
summary: Edelman Financial Engines appointed Tina Wilson as its first chief retirement officer, part of a wave of senior leadership moves among large wealth management firms this fall.

headline: Aquiline to take controlling stake in MassMutual's Flourish wealthtech platform
summary: Aquiline agreed to invest in and take a controlling interest in Flourish, the wealthtech platform MassMutual built for independent RIAs, which has grown cash-management assets under custody from $1 billion to $8 billion in five years. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026, with former Fidelity RIA chief David Canter joining as executive chairman.

headline: Global reinsurance pricing set to stay under pressure through 2027 despite healthy margins
summary: Global reinsurance pricing will keep softening through 2027, compressing underwriting margins, though healthy combined ratios and solid investment income should keep profitability above the sector's cost of capital, with cyber, renewables and data-center risk offering pockets of growth.

headline: Hong Kong pushes captive and ILS expansion to build itself as Asia's risk hub
summary: Hong Kong's Insurance Authority is advancing a five-year plan featuring a possible protected-cell structure for captives, a review of investor restrictions on ILS funds, and expanded cover for emerging sectors like gold storage and green-fuel bunkering, building on roughly $800 million in ILS issued since its dedicated regime launched in 2021.

headline: US House committee advances bill to bar CFPB from regulating insurance
summary: The House Financial Services Committee voted September 16 to advance legislation that would explicitly prevent the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau from entering state insurance regulation and require it to defer to state regulators on insurance matters.

headline: India's NeoProEd Insurance Conclave to convene sector leaders at GIFT City
summary: The NeoProEd Insurance Conclave 2026, held with the GIFT International FinTech Institute, brings together India's insurance industry leaders at GIFT City, Gandhinagar on September 25, focused on how technology, AI, data and GIFT City's growth are reshaping how insurance is built and distributed in India.

headline: Cleveland Clinic AI Summit spotlights AI's expanding clinical footprint
summary: Cleveland Clinic's annual AI Summit showcased how artificial intelligence is moving deeper into clinical workflows, from documentation and predictive analytics to imaging and operations, as health systems scale pilots into production tools.

headline: WVU Medicine set to close $800M acquisition of five-hospital Pennsylvania system
summary: WVU Health System's definitive agreement to acquire Independence Health System's five western Pennsylvania hospitals, serving more than 750,000 residents, is expected to close in late September or early October, backed by an $800 million investment commitment for a new EHR system, facility upgrades and expanded clinical capabilities.

headline: Life/annuity insurers' H1 2026 net income holds flat as pretax gains slip
summary: AM Best's midyear review found the U.S. life/annuity industry's pretax net operating gain fell 10.3% to $23.3 billion in the first half of 2026, even as total expenses declined, leaving net income roughly flat year over year.

headline: Global Atlantic debuts ForeLifetime Income fixed indexed annuity
summary: Global Atlantic launched ForeLifetime Income, a new fixed indexed annuity built for the independent marketing organization channel that aims to give savers clearer visibility into how their balance converts into guaranteed lifetime income.

headline: FIS rolls out fully cloud-native retirement recordkeeping platform
summary: FIS launched a modernized, cloud-native version of its retirement recordkeeping system, aiming to help plan providers cut infrastructure costs and speed up feature delivery as competition on recordkeeping fees intensifies.

headline: RIA M&A activity slows 19% in the third quarter
summary: Wealth management M&A activity cooled notably in Q3 2026 as market volatility prompted many advisory firm owners to delay sale processes, though analysts point to a pipeline of more than 15 deals expected to close within six months.

headline: Captrust adds $1.2 billion in double deal for two Long Island RIAs
summary: Captrust, a Raleigh-based RIA managing more than $1 trillion, acquired Compass Advisors and Long Island Wealth Management together, adding roughly $1.2 billion in client assets and seven advisors to its New York presence.

headline: Envestnet to acquire wealthtech provider Vestmark
summary: Envestnet agreed to acquire Vestmark, a portfolio management and trading technology provider supporting more than $2 trillion in assets across five million-plus accounts, bringing institutional-grade trading and tax-transition tools into Envestnet's ecosystem.

headline: Aquiline to take controlling stake in MassMutual's Flourish wealthtech platform
summary: Aquiline agreed to invest in and take a controlling interest in Flourish, a wealthtech platform currently owned by MassMutual that gives RIAs private-bank-like cash and credit solutions for clients; MassMutual will retain a minority stake.

headline: Zurich's $10.9 billion Beazley deal headlines reinsurance consolidation wave
summary: Zurich's pending $10.9 billion purchase of Lloyd's specialty (re)insurer Beazley is being cited as a bellwether for further reinsurance M&A, as surplus capital and a softening market push firms toward scale-driven consolidation.

headline: Hagerty posts H1 2026 loss on one-time Markel fronting-transition costs
summary: Specialty program administrator Hagerty reported a $5 million first-half 2026 net loss driven almost entirely by $153 million in pre-tax transitional costs as it moved to assume 100% of underwriting economics under its restructured Markel fronting arrangement.

headline: VCA Software and Vitesse link claims workflows directly to payments
summary: Claims management platform VCA Software partnered with payments infrastructure provider Vitesse so carriers, MGAs and TPAs can move a claim from approval to payout in a single workflow, removing manual re-entry for Lloyd's delegated-authority business.

headline: AI insurance startup Corgi hits $4 billion valuation in third round in eight weeks
summary: Corgi, an AI-powered commercial insurance startup, closed a Series B extension valuing the company at $4 billion, a more than sixfold jump since its January Series A, as it targets a $450 million run rate by year-end.

headline: UAE's Synapse Analytics raises $13 million for AI credit-decisioning platform
summary: Abu Dhabi-based Synapse Analytics raised a $13 million Series A led by Partech to expand its AI decisioning infrastructure, which helps banks and other regulated financial institutions automate credit, fraud and AML decisions across the Middle East, Africa and Latin America.

headline: Patra launches AI-powered managed services for insurance agencies
summary: Patra rolled out a new suite of AI-powered managed services aimed at helping independent insurance agencies automate back-office and policy servicing workflows.

headline: Peak3 launches Graphene Harness to speed insurance software delivery with AI
summary: Peak3 introduced Graphene Harness, described as the industry's first AI-driven delivery lifecycle tool for insurance technology, which the company says is already cutting build and maintenance costs by 50% with an ambition to reach 80%.

headline: UnitedHealthcare to drop prior authorization on 1,700 codes
summary: UnitedHealthcare will eliminate prior authorization requirements for 1,700 procedure codes starting October 1, spanning commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and ACA plans, as part of its pledge to cut prior-auth volume 30% by year-end.

headline: Villages Health System agrees to $541.5 million Medicare Advantage fraud settlement
summary: The Villages Health System agreed to a $541.5 million False Claims Act settlement with the Department of Justice over allegations it manufactured fake diagnosis codes for Medicare Advantage patients between 2020 and 2024, inflating payments from Humana, UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Florida.

headline: Centene's Health Net to exit commercial group market in California and Oregon
summary: Centene subsidiary Health Net is withdrawing from the traditional commercial employer-group insurance market in California and Oregon to focus on government-sponsored plans, with existing group coverage generally ending by February 2027.

headline: FTC settlement forces Caremark to overhaul PBM rebate and formulary practices
summary: The FTC secured a settlement with CVS Health's Caremark Rx and Zinc Health Services requiring changes to formulary design, rebating and vertical-integration practices, which the agency estimates could lock in up to $8.5 billion in consumer drug savings over a decade.

headline: Sanford Health and North Memorial Health finalize merger
summary: Sanford Health and North Memorial Health completed their merger, giving Sanford its first foothold in the Twin Cities and committing $600 million in Minnesota facility investment over the next decade, including preserving Robbinsdale Hospital's Level I trauma center status.

headline: WVU Health System to acquire Independence Health System's five Pennsylvania hospitals
summary: West Virginia University Health System expects to close its roughly $800 million acquisition of Independence Health System's five western Pennsylvania hospitals in late September or early October, extending its footprint to more than 750,000 residents across the region.

headline: UNC Health and Duke Health launch statewide AI network for rural hospitals
summary: UNC Health, Duke Health and partners launched NC CHAIN, a three-year, $4.4 million Duke Endowment-funded network to help rural and critical-access hospitals evaluate and safely implement AI tools they lack the in-house expertise to vet alone.

headline: Allina Health doctors reach deal after strike centered on AI oversight
summary: About 150 unionized Allina Health physicians ended a four-day strike at Mercy and Unity hospitals with a tentative first contract that includes pay transparency and greater professional autonomy, after AI's growing role in diagnosis and billing became a central bargaining issue.

headline: India's insurance stocks slide after IRDAI proposes commission caps
summary: Shares of Indian insurers and distributors, including PB Fintech, tumbled after the insurance regulator proposed caps on commissions and tighter management-expense limits, erasing roughly $13.8 billion in combined market value and raising the prospect of broker consolidation.

headline: Brussels agrees to push back high-risk AI Act rules for life and health insurance pricing to late 2027
summary: A political deal on the 'AI Omnibus' extends compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems used in life and health insurance underwriting and pricing from August 2026 to December 2027, giving insurers more runway to adapt.

headline: Advisors brace for the next wave of 401(k) recordkeeper consolidation
summary: Continued fee pressure and provider exits are pushing retirement recordkeeping toward further consolidation, creating transition risk for advisors and their plan-sponsor clients as due-diligence reviews accelerate.

headline: Savvy Wealth debuts AI-native custodial platform for independent RIAs
summary: The AI-focused wealth platform's new custodial offering lets RIA owners onboard clients in as little as 90 seconds and transfer assets in a few clicks, aiming to compete directly with legacy custodians.

headline: US P&C industry posts $31.7 billion underwriting gain in H1 2026 as premium growth cools
summary: Net income after taxes rose 53% to $77.8 billion even as net written premium growth slowed to 2.1%, with commercial rates easing for the first time in nearly nine years while casualty lines stay under pressure.

headline: Reinsurance buyers push ILS investors to broaden mandates as capacity floods the market
summary: Speaking at the Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous, Marsh Securities' CEO warned that alternative-capital investors risk losing relevance with cedents unless they widen their risk appetite in a softening reinsurance market.

headline: Palomar secures $410 million cat bond via new Torrey Pines Re vehicle
summary: The specialty P&C insurer tapped the catastrophe bond market for $410 million of reinsurance protection, adding to a record year for cat bond issuance amid abundant capacity from institutional investors.

headline: Domestic cyber claims jump 40% as years of pricing softness come to an end
summary: Nearly 50,000 cyber claims were filed in the past year as attackers shift from ransomware encryption to data-theft extortion, with analysts predicting premiums could rise 15-20% after three years of falling rates.

headline: AIG names Sierra Signorelli CEO of the Americas and global personal insurance
summary: The former Zurich executive will oversee AIG's North America, Latin America and Caribbean commercial business plus its global personal lines starting January 2027, in one of the year's biggest carrier leadership moves.

headline: HDI Global adds three underwriting and risk hires as it expands in Singapore
summary: The commercial specialty insurer strengthened its international-programmes and political-and-credit-risk teams in Singapore as it pushes further into APAC captive and renewable-energy business.

headline: PRA and FCA hold roundtable on tailored UK captive insurance regime
summary: Regulators discussed proposals for a bespoke, lower-capital regulatory track for single-parent captives, part of a UK push to become a more competitive captive insurance domicile; the consultation closes in mid-October.

headline: Sequel buys Austin-based Watkins Insurance Group as agency M&A pace cools
summary: The deal comes as US insurance-agency acquisition volume slowed roughly 15% year-over-year in the first half of 2026, according to OPTIS Partners, even as strategic and private-equity-backed buyers keep consolidating.

headline: CRC Group bundles cyber, tech E&O and professional liability into one policy form
summary: The wholesale broker's new Insurisk Cyber solution combines several specialty coverages into a single streamlined form as clients look to simplify buying amid rising cyber rates.

headline: FintechOS raises fresh funding to fund US expansion after turning profitable
summary: The financial-services technology platform, used by insurers and banks to build digital products, confirmed it turned profitable while lifting recurring revenue 40% year-on-year, and will use new capital to grow in the US.

headline: Open and Embedded Insurance Observatory convenes carriers and banks on distribution's next phase
summary: A plenary session at AWS's New York headquarters brought together AXA Partners, Allianz Partners, AIG, Swisscom, Vodafone Fastweb and others to discuss where open and embedded insurance is headed next.

headline: Soteris raises $8 million seed round to plug hidden P&C profit leaks with machine learning
summary: The YC-backed startup's round was led by Spider Capital with participation from Intact Private Capital, Amplify Partners, DCVC, the Webb Investment Network and Overlook Ventures.

headline: Indian insurtech and insurer stocks crash as IRDAI proposes sweeping distribution overhaul
summary: PB Fintech (Policybazaar) and Turtlemint Fintech tumbled roughly 20-30% after IRDAI floated capping insurer expense-of-management ratios and tightening commission and loan-bundling rules, also hitting HDFC Life and ICICI Prudential Life shares.

headline: Employers brace for a 15-year-high jump in group health benefit costs as ACA marketplace enrollment falls
summary: Purchaser surveys point to 6-7% premium increases for 2026 even as more than 1 million fewer people enrolled in ACA marketplace coverage than in 2025, a gap expected to widen as subsidy changes take hold.

headline: WVU Medicine set to close $800 million acquisition of five-hospital Independence Health System
summary: The deal, expected to close in late September or early October, will bring the combined system to 30 hospitals and more than $8 billion in annual operating revenue, with $800 million earmarked for facility upgrades.

headline: VA awards Abridge a $775 million enterprise contract for ambient clinical documentation
summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs selected Abridge's ambient AI scribe technology in one of the largest healthcare AI contracts of the year, as adoption of clinical documentation AI accelerates across large health systems.

headline: Hackensack Meridian Health completes first Joint Commission AI certification review
summary: The review covered the health system's inventory of AI tools, risk assessments, ongoing monitoring and patient-data protections, setting an early template for how hospitals will be audited on AI governance.

headline: LIMRA and LOMA launch September campaign to close the life insurance awareness gap
summary: The trade groups' Life Insurance Awareness Month push aims to educate consumers on how life coverage protects family finances, as carriers look to counter persistently stagnant ownership rates.

headline: Pooled Employer Plan adoption jumps 45% as recordkeepers make PEPs a growth priority
summary: New survey data shows 10,797 employers have now adopted PEPs for their 401(k) or 403(b) participants, up from 7,454 a year earlier, with most recordkeepers calling PEPs a major strategic priority for 2026.

headline: Swiss Re warns global catastrophe losses could hit $320 billion in a severe 2026 scenario
summary: The reinsurer's latest projection flags data-centre and renewable-energy exposures as emerging growth areas even as APAC insurers navigate a tougher catastrophe and geopolitical risk environment.

headline: European insurtech funding triples to nearly $1 billion in H1 2026
summary: Companies raised $985.9 million across 27 deals in the first half of 2026, a threefold jump versus H1 2025, with deals of $100 million or more accounting for two-thirds of the total as AI-native platforms dominate.

headline: LIMRA: Annuity sales hit new heights in the second quarter of 2026
summary: LIMRA reports Q2 2026 total annuity sales reached $123.9 billion, pushing year-to-date sales to $231.3 billion, about 2% ahead of the first half of 2025, as guaranteed income products keep gaining ground with the growing wave of Americans turning 65.

headline: PCS Retirement expands via acquisition of Aspire Financial Services
summary: PCS Retirement has agreed to acquire Aspire Financial Services, the latest in a string of recordkeeper mergers as scale becomes increasingly important for surviving margin pressure in the defined-contribution plan market.

headline: Insured Retirement Institute unveils 2026 Retirement Security Blueprint
summary: The Insured Retirement Institute released its 2026 Retirement Security Blueprint, outlining policy priorities aimed at expanding access to guaranteed lifetime income products as more Americans reach retirement age without pension coverage.

headline: Moody's: insurers set to sharply boost private credit allocations
summary: A Moody's survey finds 42% of US insurers and 36% of UK and European insurers plan to increase private credit exposure over the next one to two years, even as private credit's insurance footprint grows to roughly $1.4 trillion and sits mostly outside traditional supervisory oversight.

headline: Modern Wealth notches sixth acquisition of 2026 with California RIA deal
summary: Serial consolidator Modern Wealth has acquired AWA Wealth Management, a California-based registered investment advisor overseeing about $290 million in client assets, marking the firm's sixth acquisition of 2026.

headline: Plymouth Rock Assurance names Chris Taylor president and CEO
summary: Boston-based Plymouth Rock Assurance Corp. has named Chris Taylor as its new president and chief executive officer, a leadership change at the regional personal-lines insurer.

headline: IRDAI proposes tighter commission caps as distributor payouts outpace premiums
summary: India's insurance regulator has proposed reviving product-level commission caps and tightening insurers' overall expense limits after finding distributor payouts to agents, brokers and banks grew 259% since 2023 reforms while premiums rose just 34%.

headline: Zacks flags Willis Towers Watson, Aon, Gallagher and Brown & Brown as broker earnings momentum builds
summary: A Zacks industry outlook highlights strengthening fundamentals across major insurance brokers, with Willis Towers Watson posting a 13% rise in adjusted EBITDA and consensus estimates pointing to double-digit earnings growth across the group heading into 2026 results.

headline: Two $400 million mega-rounds anchor this week's fintech funding tally
summary: A pair of $400 million funding rounds led this week's fintech investment activity, underscoring continued investor appetite for trust-heavy sectors including insurance software, cyber and regulated financial infrastructure.

headline: AI underwriting standard-setter named to 2026 Insurtech 50 after $40 million Series A
summary: An AI-agent underwriting standards company that raised a $40 million Series A this year was named among CB Insights' 2026 Insurtech 50, reflecting a broader shift toward specialist AI underwriting startups over generalist insurtechs.

headline: Health insurance premiums on track for biggest jump in 24 years
summary: Health insurance premiums are on pace for their sharpest annual increase in 24 years, driven by rising medical costs and insurers rebuilding margins after several years of elevated utilization.

headline: IRDAI proposes sweeping overhaul of insurance distribution economics, rattling insurer and insurtech stocks
summary: India's regulator opened a consultation to cap expense-of-management ratios and agent/broker commissions and to bring more transparency to policy sales, triggering a share-price selloff at listed insurers and distributors like PB Fintech; comments are due October 25.

headline: Dai-ichi Life's New Zealand arm agrees to buy Fidelity Life for NZ$630 million
summary: Daiichi Life Group's local subsidiary Partners Life will acquire Fidelity Life Assurance, New Zealand's largest locally owned life insurer, as the Japanese group works to lift overseas business toward half of group profit by fiscal 2030.

headline: Alight names wealth solutions leader as Merit Financial Advisors hires a CTO
summary: Alight appointed Bruce Wolfe, a former Insight Investment executive, as senior vice president to lead its wealth strategy, while Merit Financial Advisors brought on John Rajes as chief technology officer to oversee its enterprise technology roadmap.

headline: Beacon Pointe adds two C-suite executives as MAP Retirement hires new plan solutions director
summary: Beacon Pointe Advisors named Katie Cullen chief growth and integration officer and Sarah Green chief risk and compliance officer, while retirement TPA MAP Retirement created a new national director of group plan solutions role for Adam Williams.

headline: UK regulators press ahead with overhaul of alternative fund manager rules
summary: HM Treasury and the FCA are advancing a coordinated package to reform the UK's regime for alternative investment fund managers, part of a broader post-Brexit push to recalibrate investment management regulation.

headline: MetLife signals strong variable investment income heading into Q3 2026 earnings
summary: MetLife told investors to expect at least $600 million in pre-tax variable investment income for the third quarter, an early positive signal for insurer general-account portfolios ahead of its November 4 earnings release.

headline: Stansberry Asset Management launches Meristead Wealth as a $1.4 billion national RIA
summary: Stansberry unveiled Meristead Wealth as its evolved national registered investment advisor brand, reflecting an expanded mandate to help clients manage, grow and preserve wealth at scale.

headline: Mercer Advisors names first chief platform officer as EP Wealth reshuffles C-suite
summary: Mercer Global Advisors appointed Goldman Sachs alum Cynthia Loh to a newly created chief platform officer role spanning technology and digital products, while EP Wealth Advisors named a new CFO and promoted its chief client solutions officer.

headline: AI tools keep expanding across advisor platforms, from document reading to opportunity discovery
summary: Betterment added an AI-powered document reader to its advisor custody platform, GReminders extended AI meeting-assistant features into Orion's Redtail CRM, and a new closed-beta tool called Trove began mining client data for growth opportunities.

headline: P&C soft market deepens as Q2 2026 premiums fall 2.0% across account sizes
summary: Carrier competition and expanded capacity pushed average commercial premium declines to their steepest pace in over a year, though commercial auto and umbrella lines remain under pressure from claims severity and litigation trends.

headline: AI data centers emerge as a new frontier for catastrophe bonds
summary: As insurers grapple with pricing risk for AI-driven data center buildouts, catastrophe bond specialists are exploring the sector as a fresh source of insurable exposure and diversification for the alternative capital market.

headline: AI-focused startups now capture the overwhelming majority of insurtech venture dollars
summary: Analysis of 2026 funding flows found roughly nine in ten venture dollars going to companies automating underwriting, claims and servicing workflows rather than traditional distribution-focused insurtech models, underscoring a decisive shift in investor priorities.

headline: CMS finalizes 2026 Medicare Advantage rules strengthening prior authorization protections
summary: The final rule restricts plans from reopening previously approved inpatient admissions except for clear error or fraud, and requires expedited coverage decisions within 72 hours and standard decisions within seven days.

headline: Heidi Health raises $340 million as valuation doubles to $900 million
summary: The Australian clinical AI startup closed a $100 million equity round led by Blackbird alongside a $240 million revenue-based growth investment from General Catalyst, funding global expansion of AI agents that handle administrative and clinical workflows under physician supervision.

headline: Catastrophe bond issuance hits a record $17.3 billion in first half of 2026
summary: Three straight years of strong returns have left reinsurance capital providers flush with capacity, and a historically light first half for insured catastrophe losses pushed 144A cat bond issuance to its highest first-half total ever.

headline: EQT to acquire specialty broker McGill and Partners in $2 billion deal
summary: Private equity firm EQT is buying a majority stake in the tech-enabled specialty (re)insurance broker, giving Warburg Pincus a full exit seven years after seeding the business, as EQT bets on McGill's data and AI-led growth strategy.

headline: TPG Growth-backed Third Wave expands into plan administration with Gulf Coast deal
summary: Retail brokerage platform Third Wave, built around Palmer & Cay, added a self-funded plan TPA capability through its Gulf Coast acquisition, reflecting a broader trend of broker platforms choosing to own administration rather than outsource it.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures unveils 2026 accelerator cohort and Global Insurance Symposium sponsorship
summary: The broker-led venture platform announced its latest startup accelerator class and confirmed sponsorship of the Global Insurance Symposium, continuing its push to connect early-stage insurance technology founders with distribution partners.

headline: InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy officially merge into India's largest AI-led distribution platform
summary: The combined entity, operating under the InsuranceDekho brand, unites InsuranceDekho's northern and western India footprint with RenewBuy's southern network, reaching over 600,000 digital partners and a premium book above Rs 6,600 crore.

headline: VA selects Abridge for enterprise ambient AI contract worth up to $775.7 million
summary: The five-year, multiple-award contract lets VA medical centers and regional networks procure Abridge's ambient clinical documentation technology, building on a pilot already deployed across more than 75 VA medical centers serving veterans in over 28 languages.

headline: Hospital margins stay squeezed in 2026 as expenses outpace revenue growth
summary: Hospital expenses rose 7.5% year over year through September, driven by competitive labor costs, while reimbursement growth failed to keep pace, leaving system-level operating margins at a modest median of 1.1% despite overall positive territory.

headline: Dai-ichi Life's NZ arm to buy Fidelity Life for NZ$630 million
summary: Dai-ichi Life's New Zealand subsidiary agreed on 3 September to acquire Fidelity Life Assurance, which would put two of New Zealand's largest life brands under one owner; closing is targeted for mid-2027 pending approvals.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable shareholders back their merger; year-end close targeted
summary: Stockholders of both companies overwhelmingly approved the plan to combine under a new parent, with closing expected by end of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals.

headline: Vanguard agrees to buy RIA custodian and platform Altruist in its largest-ever deal
summary: Vanguard will acquire Altruist, an advisor-focused custody and technology platform, for a reported $4-4.6 billion in cash, extending its push into financial advice; Altruist is to keep operating standalone.

headline: ACA insurers propose a median 15% premium increase for 2027 after enhanced subsidies lapse
summary: KFF's review of filings shows steep marketplace increases driven by medical cost growth and a shifting risk pool, raising costs even for unsubsidized middle-income buyers.

headline: Property premiums fall for a fourth straight quarter as reinsurance capital floods in
summary: A Q3 market review reports average property pricing down 6.3% in Q2, the steepest drop since 2010, while casualty stays firmer on social inflation and larger jury awards.

headline: Embedded finance revenue forecast to reach $617 billion globally by 2031
summary: A new market forecast projects strong growth in embedded finance, with B2B revenue rising sharply, reflecting the shift of payments and insurance into software workflows.

headline: Vertafore brings AI agents to independent agencies' management systems
summary: Vertafore is rolling out Velocity AI agents, including document-intelligence and coaching agents inside its agency management platforms, aimed at cutting document review and lookup time.

headline: Corgi raises $108 million and wins approval to run an AI-native carrier for startups
summary: The seed and Series A financing backs a licensed full-stack carrier using AI across underwriting, claims and policy administration; the company reports ARR above $40 million.

headline: CMS projects Medicare Advantage premiums to fall 16% in 2027
